title: Durian disease field dataset from Peninsular Malaysia, with capture-session identifiers
description:
560 field photographs of five durian disease categories, collected from commercial orchards across Peninsular Malaysia between July 2025 and June 2026, with per-image capture-session identifiers.

The session identifiers are the point of this release. The 560 images arise from only 73 reconstructed capture episodes, because a symptomatic leaf is typically photographed several times in a few seconds. Splitting at image level puts near-identical views of one specimen on both sides of a train/test boundary: 79.6% of images fall in sessions that straddle a split, and 96.7% of test images share a session with training. Group your partitions by the session column in sessions.csv.

Contents: full-resolution originals under class folders; sessions.csv mapping each (class, filename) to a session; the exact session-level 80/10/10 partition used in the paper; and the 512 px training copies used for every reported figure. Code, audit scripts and the evaluation protocol are in the accompanying repository.

Classes, with the organ photographed: Algal leaf spot (Cephaleuros virescens, leaf); Leaf rot (Colletotrichum spp. and related leaf blight, leaf); Phomopsis leaf spot (Phomopsis sp., leaf - the pathogen is also reported on fruit and stems of durian, but this dataset contains foliar symptoms only); Pink disease (Erythricium salmonicolor, branch); Root and collar rot (Phytophthora spp., trunk and collar). These are symptom classes, not confirmed aetiologies: identification rests on field-observable symptoms, with no isolation, culture or molecular confirmation and no second independent rater.

Pink disease is represented by three capture sessions across the entire collection period and its per-class metrics are not interpretable at that support. Orchard (site) identifiers were never recorded and cannot be recovered from the released files, so leave-one-site-out validation is not possible on this dataset.

Scope: the source collection also held six pest-damage categories outside the disease vocabulary under study. They are not part of this release.
notes: Group partitions by the session column. On this dataset an image-level random split leaves 96.7% of test images in a capture session that also appears in training, and inflates macro F1 by 12.2 points on average across nine architectures (range 4.9-18.4, positive in all nine), altering their rank ordering. An earlier version of this record reported 11.8 points and stated that the ranking of attention modules reverses between the two protocols; both are superseded. The reversal was an artefact of a three-seed analysis and was removed by a fourth seed - do not cite it.
